x-component

Render a template from the page or a URL into any element, fill its slots, and keep the result in the light DOM where the rest of your page can reach it.

Every section below shows the template it renders, the markup that uses it, and the live result, so nothing here needs an editor to follow. Two sections are marked Known bug and show output that is wrong today. This page is also the fixture the Playwright suite drives; csp.html and trusted-types.html cover the two scenarios it cannot.

Render a template from the page

The expression is the id of a <template> on the page. Its content is cloned into the host element and initialized against the host's scope, so item below resolves to the host's data, including inside an x-for.

Result

Style a component with the page's stylesheet

The utilities on the card below come from the page's compiled Tailwind build and are used nowhere except inside a component template. Nothing opts in: the content renders into the light DOM, so the stylesheet already applies to it. In v2 the shadow boundary cut it off, and reaching it meant naming a stylesheet with x-component-styles. This is issue #41, so this one card spells its chrome out in utilities rather than borrowing the page's .card class.

Result

Fill a component's slots

A <template x-slot> on the host fills the default <slot>, and x-slot="actions" fills the one named actions. A slot nobody fills keeps its own children as fallback. Slot content is authored on the host, so it reads and writes the host's scope: owner is the host's Ada, not the component's own value, and the button updates the host.

Result

Fill one slot from two templates

Two templates naming the same slot both fill it, in document order, the way a native slot behaves. This renders the same card as the section above.

Result

Repeat a slot for every row Known bug

A <slot> nested in an x-for or x-if template is filled, once per iteration. It is the one place slot content does not get the host's scope: the cells below ask for owner, which is Ada on the host, and render the component's component-scope instead. Alpine clones those templates with cloneNode, and the expando binding projected content to the host does not survive the clone. Keep slots out of x-for and x-if when the content needs host scope.

Result, showing the wrong scope

Swap the component at runtime

The expression is reactive. Changing it destroys the tree that was mounted and renders the new one in its place, and the host's slot content is projected again every time, including after a component that has no slots to fill. An expression that resolves to an empty string unmounts and leaves the host empty.

Result

Load a template from a URL

With the .url modifier the expression is a URL to fetch rather than the id of a template on the page. Everything else is the same, slots included. Because the fetch is asynchronous, the host emits x-component:loading and then x-component:loaded. The events bubble, so the log below listens on the wrapper rather than the host, and a same-origin URL is required unless you add .external.

Result

Reach across the component boundary

The label outside the component focuses the input inside it, that input submits with the form wrapped around the component, document queries find it, and $refs and $root resolve past the host into the surrounding tree. Every one of these was broken by the shadow boundary in v2, and together they are the reason v3 renders into the light DOM.

Result

from-host

Prove a swapped-out component is gone

The component counts its own initializations and effect runs in a store, which makes two failures visible. It initializes once and not twice, because the mount is wrapped in Alpine.mutateDom and Alpine's own mutation observer therefore leaves it alone. Swap it for the slotless card and bump the store again: the effect count holds, because the tree that left the page was destroyed rather than left running.

Result

Handle a template that will not load

Each of these leaves the host empty and reports the reason, so expect console noise from this section. A URL that fails is not cached, so retrying the same host with a working one succeeds; a cross-origin URL is blocked until you add .external, and a protocol that is not http or https is refused outright.

Throw from the component expression Known bug

When the expression itself throws, the host stays empty and no x-component:error event is emitted, so a listener waiting for one never hears about it. Alpine's evaluator catches the throw and reports it to the console out of band, which means the plugin never sees a failure to report. The failed URL in the section above does emit the event; this does not.
